memory_update.text: AEP should be kept as a reference anchor for AI data-center utility load growth because its reported large-load pipeline is unusually explicit and tied to technology customers.
POWL is a high-priority underfollowed candidate for the grid-interconnection node due to direct medium-voltage switchgear exposure, record backlog, and a disclosed large data-center order.

MYRG is a plausible underfollowed services-layer candidate because it works on transmission, distribution, substations, and data-center electrical contracting, but data-center-specific exposure needs quantification.

WCC is a second-order distribution/logistics candidate for electrical and data-center supply chains; next layer should separate gray-space power exposure from broader white-space communications exposure.

Future Layer 1B passes should also test regional utilities with high data-center load geographies, transformer-specific suppliers, power-quality equipment vendors, and nuclear fuel/services names without letting mega-cap leaders crowd out small/mid-cap discovery.

node: Grid interconnection, transmission, substations, utility power procurement and baseload availability
summary: Layer 1B expansion for the AI power bottleneck node found a two-lane universe: one regulated-utility reference anchor with unusually visible data-center load evidence, and three less-obvious public suppliers/contractors tied to the physical grid-enablement stack. The highest-evidence underfollowed candidates are Powell Industries for medium-voltage switchgear and packaged power systems, MYR Group for transmission/distribution and substation electrical construction, and Wesco for electrical distribution/logistics serving data centers, power generation, and reliability needs. Claims are research leads only, not investment recommendations.
